title: Contract Violation Root-Cause Correlation for Config/Model Deltas
creator: Ava Brooks
description:
Motivation: When a structured-output regression is detected (field missing, type drift, enum change), on-call and PMs often get an alert but lack fast grounded evidence tying the violation to a recent model or runtime configuration change. This work will build automated provenance correlation: given a set of failing samples for a contract (JSON schema / field-level invariants), produce a ranked set of likely causes (model version, quantization profile, kernel selection, batching policy, feature flag) together with precision/recall-style signals and example-level evidence for reviewers.

Goal: Ship a lightweight service that consumes sampled eval failures and configuration/model deltas and returns a ranked cause list with supporting evidence suitable for inclusion in Console alert cards and runbooks. The output must help an engineer triage within 10 minutes and provide rollback or canary suggestions where applicable.

Why different from existing detectors: many current pipelines surface violations and counts but do not correlate with the configuration change graph (time/commit/model) or produce per-sample causal evidence. This ticket focuses on correlation + explainability for structured-output regressions, not on detection thresholds themselves.
acceptance_criteria: Service ingests structured-output failure records from existing eval pipeline and links them to the model/config change graph for the last 14 days.

For a sample regression group, the service returns a ranked list of candidate causes (model version, quantization profile, runtime config flags) with a confidence score and top-3 exemplar samples supporting each cause.
Console integration: an Alert card can surface the top candidate and a short justification sentence plus link to evidence (diffed outputs, commit links).
Automated test: Synthetic regression harness where a controlled config flip (e.g., int8 quantization) produces measurable score and the system ranks that flip in top-2 candidates in >= 90% of runs.
Latency: end-to-end correlation response within 30s for typical alert (<= 200 failing samples).
steps: Design data model for failure records and change graph: unify timestamps, commit ids, model variant tags, runtime flags.
Implement lightweight correlation engine: compute temporal co-occurrence, sample overlap, and an attribution score combining effect size and exposure (heuristic + logistic regression prototype).
Add per-field attribution: measure which JSON fields' error rates shift most post-change and attach to candidate cause.
Produce evidence artifacts: sample pairs (baseline vs current), diffed JSON, short natural-language summary for Console card.
Integrate with Console alerts and eval pipeline: webhook + ephemeral evidence storage for review, include rollback/canary recommendation hints.
Create synthetic harness for int8 / kernel / batching flips and validate ranking performance, iterate on scoring weights.
Add basic permissions checks and ensure no customer PII is included in surfaced exemplars (masking rules).

2026-02-18 - Diego Patel: Spike complete: temporal co-occurrence + sample overlap heuristic identifies the culprit model in synthetic tests but struggles when multiple changes occur within the same hour. Need to add causal scoring that penalizes low-exposure changes.
2026-02-25 - PM: (Riley Chen) Reviewed design doc. Request adding example masking rules for customer data and a Console UX stub for quick triage.
2026-03-03 - Diego Patel: Prototype PR opened (link above). Contains correlation engine and simple evidence packager. Observed 92% top-2 recall in synthetic int8 flip tests (200 runs).
2026-03-09 - Security: (Maya Singh) Reviewed masking approach. Requested explicit opt-out for storing exemplars longer than 7 days; added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-12 - Diego Patel: Started Console integration; hooking into alert webhook to attach candidate list. Next: tune scoring for multi-change windows and add per-field effect size normalization.
